title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?
summary_full: Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict accessWhen Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.
